commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot from Duke to Meowmeow
commitResults.messageBody:
Renames Duke.java to Meowmeow.java and swaps the Duke-themed ASCII art
banner for a simple Meowmeow banner, since the block-letter art doesn't
scale to the new name. Updates README.md and docs/README.md (setup
steps, sample output, titles) so the docs stay in sync with the code.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-0: Greet the user and exit
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements the initial increment: print a banner/greeting on startup,
then a farewell message, matching the standard iP chatbot format
(divider lines around each block). No input handling yet.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-1: Echo user commands and exit on bye
commitResults.messageBody:
Read lines from stdin in a loop and echo each one back wrapped in
divider lines, until the user types "bye" (case/whitespace-insensitive),
at which point an ASCII cat farewell is printed and the program exits.
Scanner is opened with try-with-resources and the loop condition uses
hasNextLine() so piped input without a trailing "bye" ends the program
cleanly instead of throwing NoSuchElementException.

commitResults.messageTitle: AGENTS.md: Fill in student profile and add course constraints
commitResults.messageBody:
Records the student's actual experience level (previously placeholders)
and adds a CS2103T iP-specific constraints section — grading-relevant
repo/tag/merge rules, coding standard, build setup, reuse-credit
requirements, and the submission deadline — so future sessions don't
need to be re-briefed on them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-2: Add ability to store and list free-text items
commitResults.messageBody:
Non-command input is stored in a fixed String[100] array (per the
stage spec's <=100 item assumption) and echoed back numbered on
"list". Guards against overflow past 100 items and ignores blank
input rather than storing it as a task. Divider-boxed output is
now printed through a single printBoxed() helper instead of being
duplicated at each call site.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add present-changes-visually skill
commitResults.messageBody:
Adapts se-edu/skill-present-changes-visually for this repo: generates a
self-contained, GitHub-style split-view HTML diff of Git changes on demand.
Retargeted the skill path from .codex/skills/ to .claude/skills/ and pointed
its commit-message guidance at this project's AGENTS.md convention instead of
the (Codex-only) craft-commit-message skill. The generator script is
unmodified and uses only Python's standard library, so no dependencies are
needed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #1 from Cysiac/worktree-add-present-changes-visually-skill
commitResults.messageBody: Add present-changes-visually skill

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-3: Add ability to mark tasks as done
commitResults.messageBody:
Tracks completion with a parallel boolean[] isDone array alongside the
existing String[] items, rather than a Task class, to keep this
increment to "no new classes" as required. "list" now shows a
[X]/[ ] marker per task (and a heading line) so completion status is
visible, and a new "mark N" command flips the N-th task's marker,
with friendly errors for a non-numeric or out-of-range N instead of
crashing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-3: Add ability to reverse a task's done status
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds "unmark N", the inverse of "mark N": reverts the N-th listed
task back to not-done. Refactors the shared parse/validate/update
logic (used by both commands) into one setTaskDone(indexText, done,
...) helper instead of duplicating it, still without adding any new
classes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-3: Add Task class to represent tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Replaces the parallel String[]/boolean[] arrays (a workaround used
while the increment said "no new classes") with a Task[] of a proper
Task class in its own file, per the given partial solution:
description + isDone fields, markAsDone()/markAsNotDone(), and
getStatusIcon(). Task.toString() now owns the "[X] description"
rendering that Meowmeow previously built by hand in two places
(list, and the mark/unmark confirmation), so that formatting lives
in one spot. Output is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-2/3: Make list, add, mark, and unmark messages cat-themed
commitResults.messageBody:
The greeting and bye messages already had cat flavour ("(=^-ω-^=)",
ASCII cat, "Meow!"), but "list", the add confirmation, and the
mark/unmark confirmations were plain. Adds a light "meow" touch to
each so the persona is consistent everywhere, and reformats the add
confirmation to show the task's [ ]/[X] line the same way mark/unmark
already do, since Task now makes that easy and it matches the other
confirmations' shape.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-3: Guard bare mark/unmark, add Task.isDone() getter
commitResults.messageBody:
Typing "mark" or "unmark" with no task number fell through to the
add-task branch and got silently stored as a task literally named
"mark"/"unmark". Guards both with a friendly "which task number?"
error instead.

Also adds Task.isDone(), a plain getter for the done flag alongside
the existing getStatusIcon(), for future levels that will need the
raw boolean (e.g. saving/loading tasks).

commitResults.messageTitle: Add test-ui skill and require it after code changes
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds a console UI test runner: test/ui-test-plan.md holds test cases
(aim, input commands, expected stdout), and the test-ui skill
(.claude/skills/test-ui/) compiles the program, feeds each test
case's input to it, and stops at the first output mismatch with a
clear expected-vs-actual diff.

AGENTS.md now requires updating the test plan (if console I/O
changed) and running the test-ui skill after any change under src/,
so console-output regressions are caught before a change is
considered done rather than relying on manual spot-checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-4: Add todo command
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds "todo <description>" as an explicit command, replacing the old
behaviour where any unrecognized line was silently stored as a plain
task. Task now carries a type tag ("T") so its rendered form and the
task list show what kind of task it is, matching the course spec's
"[T][ ] description" format.

A line that doesn't match any known command now gets a friendly
guard message instead of being added as a typeless task, matching the
existing bare mark/unmark guards. Also extracts an addTask() helper
so the coming deadline/event commands don't each repeat the capacity
check and the "Now you have N tasks" confirmation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-4: Add deadline command
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds "deadline <description> /by <when>" as a second task command,
alongside "todo". Task gains a "by" field and a three-arg constructor;
toString() appends "(by: ...)" when the type tag is "D". The "/by"
marker is located with indexOf rather than split() so a missing marker
falls through cleanly into the usage-hint guard, matching the style of
the other command guards.

"by" stays a plain string for now, per the spec at this stage — no
date/time parsing yet.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-4: Add event command
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds "event <description> /from <start> /to <end>" as the third task
command. Task gains "from"/"to" fields and a four-arg constructor;
toString() appends "(from: ... to: ...)" for the "E" type. "/to" is
searched for only after "/from" is found, so text earlier in the
description can't be mistaken for the marker.

Task.java now carries four fields where any one instance uses at most
two, and toString() is a three-way if/else on the type tag - the next
commit refactors this into Task/Todo/Deadline/Event subclasses without
changing behaviour.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-4: Refactor task types into subclasses
commitResults.messageBody:
Replaces the type-tag-plus-if/else design added over the last three
commits with inheritance: Task goes back to a plain base class
(description + done status), and Todo/Deadline/Event each extend it,
overriding toString() to prepend their tag and delegate the shared
"[status] description" part to super.toString().

Meowmeow's three construction sites now call `new Todo(...)`,
`new Deadline(...)`, `new Event(...)` instead of passing a type string;
the task array stays Task[100], with no instanceof or type-checking
anywhere - each element's own toString() is picked at runtime. This is
a pure design change: all 12 UI test cases pass with byte-identical
output to the previous commit, confirming behaviour is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-4: Make deadline/event marker parsing case-insensitive and robust to duplicates
commitResults.messageBody:
Fixes two bugs found in review of the deadline/event flag parsing:

1. "/by", "/from", and "/to" were matched with plain indexOf(), which is
   case-sensitive, while the command names themselves ("deadline",
   "event") are matched case-insensitively. "/BY" was silently rejected
   as malformed. Adds a lastIndexOfIgnoreCase() helper so markers behave
   the same regardless of case.

2. indexOf() takes the first occurrence of a marker, so a description
   that happens to contain marker-like text (e.g. "reply /by email /by
   Friday") had its real flag swallowed into the description. Switched
   to searching from the end (lastIndexOf) so the marker closest to the
   end of the line - the one actually meant as the flag - wins. For
   "event", "/from" is searched for as the rightmost occurrence before
   the rightmost "/to", preserving the existing ordering requirement.

Added two test cases covering both fixes; all 14 UI test cases pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-5: Use exceptions for error handling
commitResults.messageBody:
Every error case (unknown command, bare/invalid mark or unmark target,
malformed todo/deadline/event, full task list) previously reported
itself by calling printBoxed() directly and returning early. Replace
that with a custom MeowmeowException, thrown at the point each error
is detected and caught once in the main input loop, so error reporting
is centralized instead of duplicated across every branch.

Message text is unchanged, so this is a pure control-flow refactor:
all existing UI test cases still pass byte-for-byte.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-5: Add error-handling and edge-case UI tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Add 8 test cases covering gaps in error coverage: invalid unmark
targets (previously only tested for mark), zero/negative/non-integer
mark indices, idempotent mark/unmark, deadline/event fields that are
present-but-empty, reversed event markers, blank-line input, and the
100-task capacity boundary.

Each interleaves valid and invalid commands so a rejected input's
effect on task count and list contents is checked immediately
afterward, not just that it prints an error - catching bugs where a
bad command could silently corrupt internal state even while showing
the right error message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-6: Add delete command
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds "delete N" to remove the N-th listed task by 1-based index,
mirroring the confirmation style of todo/deadline/event's add
message and reusing the index-validation guards already established
by mark/unmark (bare command, non-numeric, out-of-range). Removal
shifts the array manually to close the gap, keeping the task store a
plain array rather than introducing a Collections class.

Also updates the "unknown command" hint to list delete alongside the
other commands, and adds delete test cases to the UI test plan.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-Collections: Use ArrayList for the task store
commitResults.messageBody:
Replaces the fixed-size Task[] with an ArrayList<Task>, per the
A-Collections extension. This drops the artificial 100-task cap that
existed only because a plain array needs a fixed size on creation;
dynamic sizing is the extension's whole point, so "todo"/"deadline"/
"event" no longer have a capacity error path. deleteTask() now calls
ArrayList.remove(index) directly instead of manually shifting
elements down, and all task-count reads use tasks.size() instead of
a manually tracked taskCount variable.

Removes the "adding a 101st task is rejected" UI test, since that
capacity behaviour no longer exists; verified manually that 105 tasks
can now be added and listed without error.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-Enums: Use enums for commands, task types, and status
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduces Command, TaskType, and TaskStatus to replace three loose
representations of fixed value sets:

- Command replaces the if/else chain in main() that matched string
  literals against hand-computed substring/regionMatches offsets (e.g.
  "todo " matched at length 5 but stripped at substring(4)). Each
  constant now carries its own keyword, so the match length and the
  strip length can never drift apart, and the "unknown command" help
  text is generated from the enum's values instead of being a third,
  separately maintained copy of the same keyword list.
- TaskType moves the [T]/[D]/[E] tags out of each subclass's
  hardcoded toString() and onto one enum, which will also serve as
  the encode/decode key when Level-7 adds save-file persistence.
- TaskStatus replaces the boolean isDone flag and the boolean
  parameter to setTaskDone (now setTaskStatus), removing an
  unexplained "true"/"false" at the call site and collapsing the
  if/else that picked between the two confirmation messages.

This is a pure refactor: every line of console output is unchanged,
verified by running all 24 existing cases in test/ui-test-plan.md
with no edits to that file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-7: Save the task list to disk after every change
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a Storage class that writes the whole task list to a fixed
relative file (./data/meowmeow.txt), creating the ./data folder on
demand. Meowmeow calls Storage.save after every add, delete, mark and
unmark so the file always reflects the current list.

Each task serialises itself via a new Task.toFileString(), overridden
in Deadline and Event to append their extra fields; TaskStatus gains a
getFileFlag() ("1"/"0") so the on-disk done-flag lives next to the
on-screen icon. An IOException while saving is reported as a warning
rather than crashing the session.

Loading the file on startup is not done yet.

Also gitignore /data/ (runtime data, per-machine) and the local
.claude/worktrees/ directory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Kyqqh25LAfLVKZ7KFHkpa7

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-7: Load saved tasks on startup
commitResults.messageBody:
Meowmeow now seeds its task list from Storage.load() instead of an
empty list, so tasks entered in a previous run are still there. load()
returns an empty list when the file is absent (a normal first run),
reads it line by line otherwise, and rebuilds each Todo/Deadline/Event
from its pipe-separated fields via a private parseTask helper. A line
that does not match any known format is skipped with a warning so a
single bad line does not discard the rest.

Parsing lives in Storage (the persistence class) rather than a
Task.fromFileString factory, keeping all file-format knowledge for
reading in one place.

The UI test runner now clears ./data/ before each test case: with
startup loading in place, a data file written by one case would
otherwise leak into the next and break it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Kyqqh25LAfLVKZ7KFHkpa7

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-7: Make the data path OS-independent and tolerate a bad file
commitResults.messageBody:
Build the data-file path from separate name segments
(new Storage("data", "meowmeow.txt")) so the separator is never
hard-coded and the app works unchanged on Windows, macOS and Linux;
the path stays relative to the working directory, never machine-
specific.

Harden the load path for a first run and a corrupted file:
- a missing ./data folder is handled the same as a missing file
  (start with no tasks), and save() already creates the folder;
- parseTask now also rejects a done-flag that isn't exactly "0" or
  "1", instead of silently reading a garbled flag as "not done".

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-8: Add TaskDateTime for parsing dates and times
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce a TaskDateTime value type that turns user text such as
"2/12/2019 1800" or "2019-10-15" into a real java.time date, with an
optional time-of-day. It is a thin wrapper over LocalDate plus a
nullable LocalTime rather than a bare LocalDate/LocalDateTime, so a
user who types only a date does not get a midnight they never entered.

Parsing accepts four formats (d/M/uuuu and ISO, each with or without a
trailing HHmm) and uses ResolverStyle.STRICT so impossible dates like
30/2/2019 are rejected instead of silently rounded. The type renders
one way for the screen ("Dec 2 2019, 6:00 pm") and another, ISO-based
way for the save file, where the on-disk form is itself a valid input
format so save/load round-trips through the same parser.

Not yet wired into Deadline/Event/Storage - that follows next.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01TC12ezmdp4V7wKgddpuY3x

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-8: Store deadline/event dates as real date-times
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline.by and Event.from/to are now TaskDateTime instead of String.
The "deadline" and "event" commands parse the user's "/by", "/from" and
"/to" text into a real date on the way in and re-format it on the way
out, so "deadline return book /by 2/12/2019 1800" now lists back as
"(by: Dec 2 2019, 6:00 pm)". The existing marker-splitting logic
(rightmost marker wins, case-insensitive) is untouched - only the value
handed to the constructor changed. An event whose start is after its end
is now rejected up front.

Storage writes the ISO-based save form (2019-12-02 1800), which is
itself an accepted input format, so save/load round-trips through the
same parser. A saved line whose date no longer parses is skipped with
the existing "corrupt line" warning rather than aborting the load.

UI test plan updated: the seven cases that fed free-text dates now use
real dates, and the two usage-hint examples show a real date.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01TC12ezmdp4V7wKgddpuY3x

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-8: Handle bad date and time input gracefully
commitResults.messageBody:
Cover the error cases now that dates are parsed:

- A "/by", "/from" or "/to" value that is not a recognised date - free
  text ("tomorrow"), an impossible calendar date ("30/2/2019", caught by
  ResolverStyle.STRICT), or an impossible clock time ("2560") - prints a
  single hint listing the accepted formats and adds nothing.
- An event whose "/to" is earlier than its "/from" is refused with its
  own message.
- A saved line with an unparseable date is skipped with the existing
  "I skipped a line I couldn't read" warning (verified by hand, since
  the UI test runner wipes data/ between cases).

Two new UI test cases added for the input-side errors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01TC12ezmdp4V7wKgddpuY3x

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-8: Add an optional date filter to the list command
commitResults.messageBody:
"list" with no argument is unchanged. "list <date>" now shows only the
tasks occurring on that day: a deadline due that date, or an event whose
span covers it (so a multi-day event appears on every day it spans). A
plain todo has no date and never matches. An empty result prints its own
"free day" line rather than a bare header, and an unrecognised date
prints the same format hint as the deadline/event commands.

The matching lives in a new overridable Task.occursOn(LocalDate) -
false in Task, overridden in Deadline and Event - so the date logic
stays in the classes that own the dates, the same way toString() is
already split. The filtered view renumbers from 1 and a comment notes
those numbers are not the ones mark/delete use.

Two new UI test cases added.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch branch-Level-8
A-MoreOOP: Extract user interaction into a Ui class
commitResults.messageBody:
Meowmeow was one large class that both drove the program and formatted
every line of console output. As the first small step of the A-MoreOOP
refactor, move all user-facing input and output into a dedicated Ui
class:

* Ui owns the Scanner over System.in (hasNextCommand/readCommand) and
  implements AutoCloseable so Meowmeow can still close it via
  try-with-resources.
* Ui owns the divider, the two cat banners, and every confirmation /
  error message: showWelcome, showFarewell, showError, showAdded,
  showRemoved, showStatusChange, showTasks, showTasksOn. printBoxed and
  the singular/plural "task"/"tasks" helper are now private to Ui.
* Meowmeow's command handlers keep only the logic (parsing, list
  mutation, storage) and delegate display to a Ui passed in alongside
  the task list. listTasksOn now filters into a List<Task> and hands
  that to Ui rather than building display strings itself.

No behavioural change: console output is byte-for-byte identical and all
28 cases in test/ui-test-plan.md still pass. Command parsing and the
MeowmeowException messages are untouched; they move to a Parser class in
a later increment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01R3LrAhjfUjkoFgDa6Y2Exe

commitResults.messageTitle: A-MoreOOP: Extract the task list into a TaskList class
commitResults.messageBody:
Continue the A-MoreOOP refactor by wrapping the bare ArrayList<Task>
that Meowmeow passed between its helper methods in a TaskList class that
owns the list and the operations on it.

* TaskList offers size, add, get(int), delete(int) and findOn(LocalDate),
  all taking 1-based positions (the numbers the user sees in "list").
  get and delete validate the position and throw MeowmeowException with
  the existing "Task N doesn't exist in your list" message, so the range
  check that setTaskStatus and deleteTask each duplicated now lives in
  one place.
* asList() exposes an unmodifiable view for display and for saving, so
  the list can only be mutated through TaskList's own methods.
* Meowmeow now builds a TaskList from Storage.load() and the "list <date>"
  filter delegates to TaskList.findOn, shrinking listTasksOn to two lines.
* Storage.save widened from ArrayList<Task> to List<Task> so it accepts
  the asList() view without a copy.

No behavioural change: console output is unchanged and all 28 cases in
test/ui-test-plan.md pass. Task-number parsing and its error message
stay in Meowmeow for now; they move to a Parser class next.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01R3LrAhjfUjkoFgDa6Y2Exe

commitResults.messageTitle: A-MoreOOP: Extract command-argument parsing into a Parser class
commitResults.messageBody:
The command loop's switch inlined all the work of interpreting a
command's arguments: the empty-argument guards, the task-number parsing
(duplicated in setTaskStatus and deleteTask), and ~15 lines each of
case-insensitive "/by", "/from" and "/to" marker-splitting. Move that
into a Parser class.

* Parser.parseTaskNumber, parseTodo, parseDeadline, parseEvent and
  parseListDate turn a command's raw argument string into a ready value
  (an int, a Todo/Deadline/Event, a TaskDateTime), each raising the
  existing MeowmeowException message when the input doesn't make sense.
  lastIndexOfIgnoreCase moves in as a private helper.
* Command gains a keyword() getter so Parser can name the command
  ("mark"/"unmark"/"delete") in the "tell me which task number" message
  instead of the switch hardcoding one per case. Command still does the
  command-keyword recognition itself (Command.fromInput).
* Meowmeow's switch is now one line per command; setTaskStatus and
  deleteTask take an already-parsed int, so the Integer.parseInt block
  they each repeated is gone. Meowmeow drops from 277 to 134 lines.

No behavioural change: console output is unchanged and all 28 cases in
test/ui-test-plan.md pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01R3LrAhjfUjkoFgDa6Y2Exe

commitResults.messageTitle: A-MoreOOP: Turn Meowmeow into an instance-based skeleton
commitResults.messageBody:
Finish the A-MoreOOP refactor by reshaping the entry class to match the
assignment's sample: three collaborators held as fields, a constructor
that wires them up, a run() method with the command loop, and a one-line
main.

* Meowmeow now has final fields storage, tasks and ui. The constructor
  Meowmeow(String first, String... more) creates the Ui, gives it to a
  new Storage, and loads the TaskList; main is just
  new Meowmeow("data", "meowmeow.txt").run().
* The command loop moves into run(), which greets the user and closes
  the Ui in a finally block. The former static helpers (addTask,
  setTaskStatus, deleteTask) are private instance methods now and no
  longer thread tasks/ui through their parameter lists.
* Storage takes a Ui and reports its non-fatal warnings (unreadable
  line, failed save) through the new Ui.showWarning instead of calling
  System.out directly, so all user-facing output goes through Ui. A more
  decoupled alternative - Storage returning a result object or throwing,
  and Meowmeow deciding what to show - was left out as more code than
  this project needs.

Divergence from the sample: there is no try/catch around the load,
because Storage.load handles a missing or partly-corrupt file itself
(start empty / skip only the bad lines) rather than throwing.

No change to normal console output; all 28 cases in
test/ui-test-plan.md pass. A load warning on a corrupt file now prints
just before the welcome banner (the constructor loads before run()
greets), matching the sample's ordering.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01R3LrAhjfUjkoFgDa6Y2Exe

commitResults.messageTitle: A-MoreOOP: Rename the Command enum to CommandType
commitResults.messageBody:
The stretch goal introduces an abstract Command class with AddCommand,
DeleteCommand etc. as subclasses. That class wants the name "Command",
so free it up first: the keyword enum from the A-Enums increment becomes
CommandType, sitting alongside the existing TaskType and TaskStatus
enums.

Pure rename via git mv (history follows the file). fromInput, matches,
argumentsOf, keyword() and helpText() are unchanged; the three
references in Meowmeow.java and Parser.java are updated. No behavioural
change - all 28 cases in test/ui-test-plan.md pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01R3LrAhjfUjkoFgDa6Y2Exe

commitResults.messageTitle: A-MoreOOP: Replace the command switch with a Command class hierarchy
commitResults.messageBody:
The stretch goal for A-MoreOOP: turn each command into its own object so
the main loop is just parse -> execute -> check-for-exit, with no switch.

* New abstract Command with execute(TaskList, Ui, Storage) and isExit()
  (default false). Concrete subclasses AddCommand, DeleteCommand,
  MarkCommand, ListCommand and ExitCommand each hold their parsed values
  as final fields; their execute bodies are the former private helpers of
  Meowmeow (addTask / deleteTask / setTaskStatus), moved verbatim.
* Grouping: one AddCommand for todo/deadline/event (Parser already builds
  the right Task subclass, so "add" is identical); one MarkCommand for
  mark/unmark carrying a TaskStatus (matching how TaskStatus already
  unifies those two paths); ListCommand uses a nullable TaskDateTime
  field (null = list everything) instead of a second class.
* Parser gains a single entry point, parse(String) -> Command: it does
  the CommandType recognition, then a switch that *builds and returns*
  the right Command instead of *doing the work*. parseTaskNumber,
  parseTodo, parseDeadline, parseEvent are now private helpers of parse;
  parseListDate is inlined. All MeowmeowException messages are unchanged.
* Meowmeow.run() drops to the target shape - a while (!isExit &&
  hasNextCommand()) loop around Parser.parse / command.execute /
  command.isExit. The switch, the labelled break and the three private
  helpers are gone; Meowmeow is now 72 lines. The hasNextCommand() guard
  (graceful EOF) and the blank-line skip are kept even though the
  assignment's sample loop omits them.

No behavioural change: console output is unchanged and all 28 cases in
test/ui-test-plan.md pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch branch-A-MoreOOP
A-Packages: Organize classes into Java packages
commitResults.messageBody:
Move all 20 source classes out of the default package into a
`meowmeow` package hierarchy, one sub-package per role:

  meowmeow          app entry point (Meowmeow) + shared MeowmeowException
  meowmeow.ui       Ui
  meowmeow.storage  Storage
  meowmeow.parser   Parser, CommandType
  meowmeow.task     Task/Todo/Deadline/Event, TaskList, TaskType,
                    TaskStatus, TaskDateTime
  meowmeow.command  Command + AddCommand/DeleteCommand/ExitCommand/
                    ListCommand/MarkCommand

The flat default package had grown to the point where parsing,
storage and domain classes were indistinguishable neighbours;
grouping them by responsibility makes the design visible from the
directory tree and prepares the repo for the A-Packages increment.

MeowmeowException stays at the top level because parser, task,
command and storage all throw it, so it belongs to no single one.
CommandType goes with the parser because its job is recognising
which keyword was typed, not executing it.

src/main/java remains the source root (required by later tooling).
The change is limited to `package` declarations plus the `import`
statements each cross-package reference now needs; no member
visibility was widened (a scan found no package-private members).
A few comment-only {@link}s to now-foreign classes were switched to
fully-qualified links so no unused import is left behind.

Test tooling updated for the nested layout: the test-ui skill's
compile command now recurses into sub-directories, and the runner's
default main class is `meowmeow.Meowmeow`. Console I/O is unchanged,
so test/ui-test-plan.md needs no edits; all 28 UI test cases pass.
